Thank you for your understanding. 9/9 EVR Gallery The Leqtique 9/9, released in 2013, has been manufactured and sold as our brand's best-selling distortion model for a long time. 12 years have passed since then, but the only distortion pedals that use the four-stage depletion type MOSFETs that make up the 9/9 as the sole distortion element are this pedal, the 10/10, and its variations (6/6, etc.). The technique of using a type of transistor called a FET as a substitute for vacuum tubes in an amplifier circuit is now widely used because it produces a circuit and sound that is significantly different from those that use opamp elements, which is the most common method of making distortion effects. MOSFETs generally operate in what is known as an enhancement type mode, which means that they behave fundamentally differently from FETs, so the technique described above cannot be used. However, Depletion type MOSFETs, although very few in number, are becoming more common in the electronic components industry in the 2010s, and they share many behaviors with FETs, making it possible to similarly configure a multi-stage distortion circuit by treating a single element like an ultra-small vacuum tube. When using MOSFETs to create distortion effects, they do not have the ultra-low noise of FETs, but the biggest advantage I discovered was the balance of the second and third harmonics they produce. (Although this also varies greatly depending on the operating point at which the elements are used.) A multi-stage distortion circuit section made up of DMOSFETs has more second harmonics than a similarly constructed FET, which contributes greatly to making the 9/9 sound tight yet mellow. The 9/9 was created as such a "Harmonic High Gain Distortion", but in fact it was by far the longest circuit design for Leqtique pedals, and even though 12 years have passed, there are no fundamental changes that could be made, and in this EVR update, the operating points of each distortion section have been exquisitely adjusted (no major sound changes at all), and the Treble control has been influenced by the subsequent 10/10 and 11/11, expanding it to a fairly wide range. This is similar to the RED → RED EVR update, but the range of more harmonic lead sounds, tight and sharp riffing, and chord work sounds has been expanded. As was the case during the Leqtique era, the 9/9 EVR is the flagship distortion model of the Leqtique EVR line, and is especially recommended for users who like the Leqtique 10/10 11/11, as it helps understand the brand concept. *All controls are the same as the original Leqtique 9/9, including a Mid Control inside. Shun Nokina About the "EVR" concept Since 2019, I have been based in Europe and have been involved in the design of several pedals, but Leqtique pedals have been essentially on hiatus without releasing any new products. However, by temporarily relocating to Iceland in 2024, I was able to get some great inspiration, and I have continued to design all of them as an update package called "EVR". "EVR" means EVRU: Europe in Icelandic. The letters strongly express the idea of ​​feeding back and embodying the inspiration and experiences gained in various parts of Europe over the years as a base or commuter. Leqtique pedals originally embodied a strong longing for Europe, such as the color of the paint and the darkness of the sound, but now they are clearly embodied as a more realistic experience. Leqtique pedals have not been updated for 15 years, but we have completely reconstructed the case, all components, concept, etc. from scratch.
